name: In-house legal review of a sales contract on the customer's paper
summary: A customer sends its own form of agreement for a software or services purchase, and the company's in-house legal team has to turn it into terms the company can accept. The account executive opens a legal request, a contracts manager triages it, commercial counsel reviews the document against the playbook and sends redlines, and finance, sales leadership and sometimes the general counsel approve terms outside the standard positions. The draft then goes back and forth with the customer's lawyers for one to three rounds before a clean version is signed by both sides and filed. Most of the elapsed time is waiting: in the legal queue, for approvers, and above all for the customer's own legal and procurement staff.

baseline.org_archetype: A US software or IT services company selling to business customers, with a legal team of five to ten people and a contracts manager, using a CRM, email, Word and e-signature.
baseline.notes: Covers only contracts where the customer insists on its own paper and the deal is large enough for legal to negotiate it; standard click-through and template deals are excluded.

unit_of_work: one sales contract on the customer's paper (master agreement or services agreement with its order form)
trigger: The account executive receives the customer's form of agreement and opens a legal request on the CRM opportunity.
end_state: The agreement is signed by both parties, the deal is booked and the executed contract is filed with its key terms recorded, or the deal is abandoned during negotiation.

volume.seasonality: Peaks in the last two to three weeks of each fiscal quarter and especially the fiscal year end, when sales push deals to close.

evidence.note: Estimate for a 1,000-employee software company. ACC 2019 reports a median of 300 contracts of all types reviewed per legal department per year; customer-paper sales contracts are a minority of these.

triggered_by.object: customer contract draft with order form
customer contract draft sent directly to legal

produces.object: stalled or lost deal with negotiation history

systems.name: CRM with legal request and deal approval objects
Word processor with track changes and document compare
Contract repository (shared drive or basic contract management tool)
Contract playbook and approval matrix (document or wiki)

steps.name: Open legal request with customer paper
steps.description: The account executive receives the customer's master agreement or services agreement by email, opens a legal request on the CRM opportunity, attaches the customer document and any order form or statement of work, and fills in deal value, products, deadline and the customer contacts.

error.defect_description: Missing order form, wrong customer legal entity, or deal value and deadline left blank.

evidence.note: GitLab describes opening a legal case on the opportunity with documents, details and deadline. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Triage request and check completeness
steps.description: The contracts manager reviews the new request in the legal queue, checks that the customer document, order form, deal value and deadline are present, logs the matter in the tracker, sets a priority based on deal size and quarter end, and either assigns a counsel or returns the request for missing information.

error.defect_description: Wrong priority or assignment to a counsel without capacity.

control.basis: Legal intake policy: requests only through the CRM legal case with required fields; negotiation thresholds by deal size

next.condition: returned to the account executive for missing documents or details

evidence.note: GitLab describes a queue with assignment and an automated message listing required documents. The 15% return rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Look up existing agreements and customer history
steps.description: The contracts manager searches the repository and the CRM for an existing NDA, prior master agreement, earlier redlines or past concessions with this customer or its parent company, and attaches anything found to the request so counsel does not start from nothing.

error.defect_description: A prior agreement or earlier concession is not found because files are misnamed or saved outside the repository.

evidence.note: DocuSign 2019 reports 39% of contracting staff could not locate contracts they searched for and 31% track contracts in spreadsheets. Times are estimates.

steps.name: First full review against the playbook
steps.description: Commercial counsel reads the customer's agreement clause by clause and compares it with the company playbook: limitation of liability, indemnities, intellectual property, warranties, service levels, data protection, payment, termination, audit rights and governing law. Counsel notes each deviation, its risk and the fallback position allowed.

error.defect_description: A non-standard clause such as a most-favoured-customer price, uncapped data breach liability or an acceptance test is missed.

evidence.note: Queue wait reflects UTSA's 6 to 14 business days to first full review for non-standard agreements and Lexion's finding that most legal teams report reviews within five days. Hands-on time is an estimate.

steps.name: Answer legal's business questions
steps.description: The account executive answers counsel's questions about scope, service levels, pricing, implementation services and what was promised to the customer, often after checking with the customer or a solutions engineer, and replies in the CRM case or by email.

error.defect_description: The answer omits a side promise such as a roadmap commitment or custom service level.

next.condition: customer paper includes security, privacy or data processing terms needing specialist review

evidence.note: Typical practice for customer paper at software companies. The 55% share with security or data terms reflects that most software and services deals involve customer data; estimate.

steps.name: Security and privacy review of data terms
steps.description: The security and privacy analyst reviews the customer's security exhibit, data processing terms and any audit, breach notice or data location requirements against the company's actual controls and certifications, and marks what the company can and cannot commit to.

error.defect_description: A commitment the company cannot meet, such as a 24-hour breach notice or a data location promise, is accepted.

control.basis: Information security policy: customer security and data processing commitments reviewed by security; data processing terms needed where the company processes personal data for the customer

evidence.note: UTSA names information security as a secondary review that lengthens time to execution. Times and share are estimates.

steps.name: Draft redlines and internal issues summary
steps.description: Counsel marks up the customer's document in track changes with explanatory comments, inserts the company's positions on each issue, and writes a short internal summary of open points and of any terms that fall outside the playbook fallbacks.

error.defect_description: Edits made without track changes or inconsistent defined terms across sections.

evidence.note: Redlining customer paper with extensive modifications is described by GitLab. Hands-on time is an estimate.

steps.name: Check deviations against the approval matrix
steps.description: Counsel compares the proposed positions with the approval matrix to see which deviations need business, finance or general counsel approval, such as payment terms beyond 60 days, liability above the standard cap, termination for convenience or acceptance clauses.

error.defect_description: A deviation that needs approval is not routed.

next.condition: one or more deviations need approval

evidence.note: Approval matrices for non-standard terms are common practice; the 40% share needing approval at first markup is an estimate.

steps.name: Enter exception request in the deal approval form
steps.description: The deal desk analyst copies the non-standard terms from counsel's summary into the CRM deal approval form, adds deal value, margin and payment schedule, and routes it to the approvers the matrix names.

error.defect_description: Terms re-keyed incorrectly from the legal summary into the approval form.

control.basis: Deal desk approval matrix for non-standard commercial terms

evidence.note: Re-keying from legal documents into a CRM approval form reflects common 2019 to 2022 tooling; times are estimates.

steps.name: Finance and revenue accounting review
steps.description: The finance manager reviews payment terms, acceptance, termination rights, service credits and any penalties or price protections for their effect on cash flow and on revenue recognition, then approves, approves with conditions, or rejects with a counter-position.

error.defect_description: Revenue effect of a termination or acceptance clause misjudged.

control.basis: Revenue recognition policy under ASC 606 and internal control over financial reporting: accounting review of non-standard terms before execution

next.condition: rejected; counsel must change the position

evidence.note: Forvis Mazars says legal and accounting should both review proposed changes before execution. DocuSign 2019: 84% say approvals have stalled deals. Wait and rejection rate are estimates.

steps.name: Sales leadership approval of business terms
steps.description: The vice president of sales reviews the commercial concessions such as service credits, extended payment terms or price holds against the deal's value and approves or declines in the CRM, sometimes after a call with the account executive.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Deal desk approval matrix: sales leadership approves commercial concessions above thresholds

next.condition: legal risk deviation needs general counsel approval

evidence.note: Runs in parallel with the finance review in most companies, so the wait is short; shares are estimates.

steps.name: General counsel approval of legal risk escalation
steps.description: The general counsel reviews the escalation memo for deviations such as uncapped liability, broad intellectual property indemnities or unusual audit rights, weighs them against deal value and strategic importance, and approves, sets a limit, or refuses.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Contract playbook escalation rules: deviations beyond fallback positions need general counsel approval

next.condition: refused or limited; position must change

evidence.note: GitLab describes an escalation process for material non-standard terms to leadership. Times and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Send redlines to the counterparty
steps.description: Counsel sends the redlined draft with a cover note explaining the main changes to the customer's procurement or legal contact, copying the account executive, and records the version sent in the CRM case.

error.defect_description: Wrong version or a draft with internal comments is sent.

evidence.note: DocuSign 2019 reports 80% share contracts by email and almost 30% have sent a contract to the wrong party. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Counterparty reviews and responds
steps.description: The customer's procurement and legal staff review the redlines in their own queue, consult their business owner and return a revised draft, often with some changes not tracked, or ask for a call.

error.defect_description: Counterparty changes made without track changes.

evidence.note: UTSA says time after first review depends mostly on the other party's flexibility and response time. The 1 to 21 day spread is an estimate.

steps.name: Review counterparty response and compare versions
steps.description: Counsel runs a document compare against the last version sent, reads every change including untracked ones, decides which customer positions fit within the playbook fallbacks, and decides whether terms are agreed, need another round, or need a new approval.

error.defect_description: An untracked counterparty change is missed in the compare.

next.condition: open issues within authority; another round needed
customer demands a concession that needs new approval
deal lost or abandoned during negotiation

evidence.note: DocuSign 2019: 52% say contracts go through three to four versions before signing, which the loop probabilities reproduce (about 1.9 counterparty turns on average). Shares are calibrated estimates.

steps.name: Negotiation call with the counterparty
steps.description: Counsel and the account executive schedule and hold a call with the customer's counsel and procurement to work through the remaining issues, trading positions within the fallbacks and noting agreed wording.

error.defect_description: Agreement on the call recorded differently by each side.

evidence.note: Scheduling a call across two legal teams and sales typically takes several days; estimate.

steps.name: Revise draft after negotiation
steps.description: Counsel updates the draft to reflect what was agreed on the call, adjusts related clauses for consistency, and decides whether any concession now needs approval before the draft goes back to the customer.

error.defect_description: Change made in one clause but not in a related definition or exhibit.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Prepare execution version
steps.description: The contracts manager accepts all changes, removes comments, checks that the customer legal entity, addresses, dates, exhibits and order form match the agreed terms, and saves a clean execution version as a PDF.

error.defect_description: Wrong exhibit version or blank left unfilled.

evidence.note: Estimate based on common practice.

steps.name: Final legal approval of the execution version
steps.description: Counsel opens the execution version, spot-checks the agreed changes and the order form, and applies the legal approval in the CRM case so the document may be sent for signature.

error.defect_description: An error in the execution version passes.

control.basis: Legal sign-off policy: all agreements need legal approval on the document before signature

evidence.note: GitLab requires a legal approval stamp on all agreements before signature. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Booking check of order form against contract
steps.description: The deal desk analyst compares the order form, quote and approved exceptions with the final contract terms, checking price, payment terms, term length and billing dates, so the deal can be booked without later revenue or billing corrections.

error.defect_description: A mismatch between quote and contract is missed.

control.basis: Quote-to-cash booking control: signed terms must match approved pricing and exceptions (internal control over revenue)

evidence.note: Common revenue control at software companies; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Set up the e-signature envelope
steps.description: The account executive creates the e-signature envelope from the CRM, adds the customer signer first and the company's authorized signatory second, and copies counsel and the contracts manager.

error.defect_description: Wrong signer or signing order chosen.

evidence.note: GitLab describes sales sending agreements for signature by DocuSign from the CRM. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Customer signs
steps.description: The customer's authorized signer receives the envelope and signs, which may wait for the customer's own internal approvals, purchase order or supplier registration before the signature is applied.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: customer asks for a last-minute change

evidence.note: DocuSign reports 79% of agreements signed within 24 hours; the long tail reflects customer purchasing approvals. Estimate for the tail.

steps.name: Authorized officer countersigns
steps.description: The company's authorized signatory, usually the chief financial officer or a delegate named in the signature authority matrix, opens the envelope, checks the legal approval and deal value, and signs.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Delegation of signature authority: sales staff may not sign; only officers in the authorization matrix sign customer agreements

evidence.note: GitLab: no one in sales is authorized to sign; only individuals in the authorization matrix may execute. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Book the deal and update billing terms
steps.description: The deal desk analyst marks the opportunity closed-won, attaches the executed agreement, and re-keys the term dates, payment terms, billing schedule and any service credit obligations into the billing system so invoicing follows the contract.

error.defect_description: Payment terms or billing dates keyed incorrectly in the billing system.

control.basis: Revenue and billing controls: booked order must be supported by an executed contract

evidence.note: Re-keying contract terms into billing systems was common before integrated quote-to-cash tools; times are estimates.

steps.name: File executed contract and record key terms
steps.description: The contracts manager saves the executed agreement in the repository under the customer name, enters metadata such as term, renewal, liability cap, notice periods and non-standard obligations in the tracker, and closes the legal case.

error.defect_description: Metadata incomplete or wrong, so renewal or obligation dates are later missed.

control.basis: Contract record retention policy; external auditors request executed contracts when testing revenue

evidence.note: GitLab asks that executed agreements be sent to legal for the contract system; DocuSign 2019 reports 31% manage contracts in spreadsheets. Filing backlog wait is an estimate.

exceptions.name: Missing intake information
exceptions.description: The request lacks the order form, deal value or the customer's legal entity and goes back to the account executive before triage can finish.

exceptions.name: Security and data processing terms
exceptions.description: The customer's paper includes a security exhibit or data processing terms that the security and privacy analyst must review before counsel can finish the redlines.

exceptions.name: Escalation to general counsel
exceptions.description: The customer demands uncapped liability, broad indemnities or unusual audit rights, which need finance, sales and general counsel approval before counsel can respond.

exceptions.name: Approver rejects proposed position
exceptions.description: Finance, sales leadership or the general counsel refuses a concession, so counsel must redraft and the approval runs again on the next round.

exceptions.name: Deal lost or abandoned in negotiation
exceptions.description: The customer chooses another vendor or the deal stalls past the quarter, and the legal case is closed without signature.

exceptions.name: Last-minute change at signature
exceptions.description: The customer's signer or procurement asks for a change after the envelope is sent, which reopens review and voids the envelope.

exceptions.name: Booking mismatch
exceptions.description: The deal desk finds that the quote, approvals and contract disagree on price, term or payment terms and the execution version is corrected before signature.

assumptions: The company is a mid-size US software or services vendor of about 1,000 employees with five to ten in-house legal staff; the process is the customer-paper path only.
Volume of 18 customer-paper contracts a month is an estimate; companies with strict negotiation thresholds see fewer, enterprise-focused vendors see more.

Branch probabilities for approvals, negotiation rounds and abandonment are the author's estimates calibrated so the average number of versions matches the DocuSign 2019 finding that half of contracts go through three to four versions.

The cycle-time benchmark is a synthesis: published medians of 15 days (ACC 2019, APQC) cover all contract types including simple templates, and the 50-day Ironclad figure is a mean for complex technology master agreements; the simulated median of about 40 days sits between them, which fits the customer-paper case.
Approvals by finance and sales leadership are modelled as running in parallel (short wait on the second approver); companies that route them one after another will see longer cycles.
The process ends when the executed contract is filed; filing can lag signature by days, so cycle time to signature is a few days shorter than the simulated figure.

Hands-on times for counsel (about 12 hours per contract including rounds) are estimates; DocuSign 2019 reports a third of respondents say a typical contract takes more than 30 hours to negotiate across all parties.
Loaded costs use BLS May 2021 wages times about 1.7 (benefits factor 1.44 from BLS ECEC plus about 20% overhead, the author's estimate).
Several sources are vendor surveys or post-2022 publications (Lexion 2023, Ironclad 2025); they are used as indications of typical practice in the reference period.
